title: Randolph Park master-plan geometry is preserved
summary: City plan L-63-006 preserves the 1963 Randolph Park master-plan and drainage geometry. It predates both the City’s later band-stage chronology and the recovered BMX evidence, so it serves only as an earlier spatial-control layer.

title: City records a Band Enclosure at Randolph Park
summary: City construction-plan metadata identifies C-66-003 as “Band Enclosure @ Randolph Park.” The drawing is not scanned in the archive, so only the cataloged title and date are admitted.

title: Randolph Park is renamed Reid Park
summary: Pima County Public Library’s local-history file says the park now known as Reid Park was originally Randolph Park and received the Reid Park name in 1978. This is park-name context, not proof of a BMX-track rename or exact footprint.

title: Debbi Kalsow's documented competition span
summary: Kalsow's 2018 Hall of Fame profile says she competed from 1979 through 1985, a span that includes her Arizona district and national-title years.

title: Chino Valley acquires Old Home Manor
summary: Chino Valley’s adopted 2014 General Plan says the Town acquired the more-than-800-acre Old Home Manor property in 1979. The acquisition anchors later site history but does not backdate BMX activity to 1979.

title: Kalsow becomes ABA National No.1 Girl
summary: Her official profile records 1982 as her ABA National No.1 Girl season and says it was the first year ABA awarded that national girls title.

title: Kalsow records NBL National No.1 Girl Pro
summary: Debbi Kalsow's Hall of Fame profile records her as 1984 NBL National No.1 Girl Pro.

title: Pete Kelley enters the National BMX Hall of Fame
summary: USA BMX's 2024 Debbie Kelley profile identifies Pete Kelley as a National BMX Hall of Famer inducted in 1995.

title: Federal Register identifies London Bridge BMX Association
summary: The Federal Register identifies Frank Sabatano as President of the London Bridge BMX Association in comments addressing bicycle racing and jumping safety.

title: Hayashi wins back-to-back National No.1 Girl Cruiser titles
summary: Hayashi's official profile records National No.1 Girl Cruiser titles in 2000 and 2001.

title: Hayashi records five consecutive NBL No.1 Elite Women titles
summary: Kim Hayashi's official profile credits her with five consecutive NBL No.1 Elite Women titles from 2003 through 2007.

title: USA BMX headquarters moves to Tulsa
summary: USA BMX reported that its new headquarters moved to Tulsa's Greenwood District in February 2022.

title: Kim Hayashi remains involved as a coach and team manager
summary: USA BMX's 2024 Hall of Fame profile says that after retiring from the pro circuit, Kim Hayashi remained involved in BMX as a coach and team manager.
